summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 58 (ipns-signature-verify-coverage) of the CipherBox project using the GSD workflow system, including automated research, plan generation, verification, and wave-based execution.
summary.outcome: Planning completed cleanly (4 plans, 2 waves, 0 blockers). Execution reached 3/4 plans confirmed complete (58-01 after crash recovery, 58-02, 58-03), with 58-04 spawned but result unknown at transcript end.

repo: crates/crypto cannot dev-depend on api-client/core, so cross-language Rust verify vectors must live in crates/fuse/tests/ rather than crates/crypto/tests/ to avoid a dependency cycle.
The full-SDK-E2E gate for sequence-enforcement changes is historically high-risk: a prior similar change-class broke 48/89 SDK E2E tests.
Local dev stack runs redis on :6380, API on :3000, with docker compose managing postgres and ipfs/kubo — all were up during this session.
RESEARCH.md open-questions sections require an explicit (RESOLVED) marker after questions are handled in-plan, or the plan checker emits a warning.
resolve_ipns_verified is the new Rust verification chokepoint in crates/fuse that all 9 FUSE resolve sites now route through.
The GSD commit helper reports commit_failed as a known false negative; always verify with git log rather than retrying the commit.
AUTO_MODE=true combined with a live local stack allows E2E gates to run automatically without human prompts.
VALIDATION.md frontmatter must be written by the orchestrator; body scaffold is owned by execute/validate tooling.

code.finding: ciborium is listed as a dependency of the fuse crate; a mid-crash diagnostic incorrectly flagged it as missing because it read a stale/partial state.
expectedSequenceNumber guard is the CAS 409 conflict check and was intentionally preserved — it is not part of the D-09 non-CAS sequence enforcement gate.

workflow: Sequential subagent execution on a shared feature branch is safer than parallel worktree isolation for crypto/security phases where merge conflicts and cwd-drift risks outweigh speed gains.

When an executor agent dies mid-run due to an API socket error, the git log is the authoritative state source — completed commits survive and a continuation agent can resume from that point without replanning.
An executor subagent can overrun its assigned plan boundary and complete the next plan in the same run; always check git log and SUMMARYs before assuming only one plan was touched.

The SDK E2E gate can silently skip if the API process on :3000 was started from compiled dist with a mismatched TEST_LOGIN_SECRET — the gate 401s on test-login and marks itself infra-limited rather than failing.
The GSD plan-checker will pass on cosmetic warnings (e.g., missing RESOLVED markers) without requiring a full planner re-run; fix the doc directly and commit.

friction: 58-01 executor died mid-task-4 due to an API socket connection-closed error, leaving Task 3 done-but-uncommitted and Task 4 unstarted, requiring a manual recovery continuation agent.
58-02 executor overran into 58-03 and completed both plans in one agent run, making orchestrator plan-tracking ambiguous until git log was checked.

58-02's mandatory full-SDK-E2E gate did not actually execute: the API on :3000 was started from compiled dist with a mismatched TEST_LOGIN_SECRET, causing test-login to 401 and the suite to skip entirely.
RESEARCH.md open-questions lacked (RESOLVED) markers, causing a plan checker warning that required a direct doc edit + commit cycle.
